title: Effect of uniform bond-charge order on longitudinal spin-susceptibility jump at a superconducting instability inside a magnetic phase
abstract: A previous work [H. Yamase and M. Zafur, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{103}, 224527 (2021)] showed that the longitudinal spin susceptibility exhibits a jump when the superconductivity develops continuously inside a magnetic phase. That analysis employed a minimal model containing magnetic and superconducting interactions. However, in correlated-electron systems, both magnetic and bond-charge interactions originate from the same underlying spin-spin exchange interaction. We therefore extend the model by including the uniform bond-charge order to provide a more realistic description of the system. We find that the jump of the longitudinal spin susceptibility remains robust even in the presence of uniform bond-charge order, but the uniform bond-charge order quantitatively enhances the longitudinal spin susceptibility and the size of the jump at $T_c$.
summary: This theoretical study examines the longitudinal spin susceptibility jump at a superconducting instability within a magnetic phase, extending the model to include uniform bond-charge order. Using mean-field theory, the authors find that while the bond-charge order does not eliminate the jump, it significantly enhances both the susceptibility and the jump magnitude. This confirms the robustness of the jump mechanism tied to the superconducting response in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the longitudinal spin susceptibility jump that occurs when superconductivity develops within a magnetic phase, extending previous models by incorporating uniform bond-charge order.
main_result: The jump in the longitudinal spin susceptibility remains robust despite the inclusion of bond-charge order, which quantitatively enhances both the susceptibility and the jump size at the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$).
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory (RPA) applied to an effective square-lattice Hamiltonian, calculating the grand-canonical potential and deriving self-consistency equations for the order parameters.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using an effective square-lattice Hamiltonian containing kinetic, magnetic, bond-charge, and superconducting interaction terms. It describes correlated-electron systems exhibiting coexistence of magnetic and superconducting orders.
key_observables: Longitudinal spin susceptibility ($\chi_n$), superconducting order parameter ($\Delta_0$), magnetic order parameter ($m$), and bond-charge order ($\chi_b$).
important_parameters: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), magnetic transition temperature ($T_N$), and the applied magnetic field ($h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory, assumes a uniform bond-charge order ($\chi_x = \chi_y = \chi_b$), and compares results derived from fixed-density versus fixed-chemical-potential ensembles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing how bond order suppresses magnetism and affects $T_N$ and $T_c$, and show the temperature dependence of $\chi_\mu$ comparing results with and without bond order.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work by extending the model Hamiltonian to include bond-charge order. It then calculates the longitudinal spin susceptibility using linear response theory by differentiating the self-consistency equations with respect to the external field $h$, analyzing the resulting jump at $T_c$ and comparing fixed-density vs. fixed-$\mu$ results.
why_interesting: The investigation into field-induced responses and the persistence of singular behavior (the jump) in the presence of multiple competing orders (magnetism, superconductivity, charge order) is highly relevant to understanding complex quantum materials.
